Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references attacks and incidents spanning 2011–2024
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — ongoing pattern of suspected sabotage implies continued near-term risk to Bulgarian arms/industrial sites
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — persistent alleged Russian sabotage campaign with no resolution signals enduring geopolitical risk

Synopsis:
    A second explosion hit an EMCO-operated weapons storage facility in central Bulgaria (near Tsareva Livada, Gabrovo region) overnight on 12 September 2026, causing fires that spread across multiple warehouses. No casualties were reported. EMCO, controlled by arms trader Emilian Gebrev, has a documented history of alleged Russian-linked sabotage operations targeting its munitions depots, which store arms destined for Ukraine and Georgia. Bulgarian authorities issued arrest warrants for six Russian nationals in 2024 in connection with prior depot destructions (2011–2020). The pattern of incidents is linked by prosecutors to a broader Russian covert disruption campaign, also tied to Czech munitions depot explosions in 2014 and an attempted poisoning of Gebrev in 2015. Moscow denies involvement.
